Read from gpuBackdrop.fx. Dark + Compact + Full clicked on /settings survived a reload and rendered as pressed; no console errors.

/settings — desktop 1440×1000

  • Before: no such page, so the app’s own 404.
  • After: one card, four rows — Theme, Density, Sound, Effects — each a segmented control with the simplest choice selected by default.
  • Header gains a Settings link (it was the deleted page’s main flaw that only Ctrl+K reached it).

/settings — mobile 390×844

  • Each row wraps: copy above, choices below. Nothing overflows the card at 390px.

/ — desktop 1440×1000

  • Only the nav moved: Settings added after Users (pixel diff confined to the header bar).
  • The Three.js starfield behind this page is gone; on a GPU machine / now draws the same shared backdrop as every other page. (These captures have no GPU, so both show the CSS fallback.)

/ — mobile 390×844

  • Pixel-identical: the nav collapses into the drawer at this width.

/azure — desktop 1440×1000

  • Settings link in the header.
  • Small text now resolves from the type ladder instead of raw rems: “Updated 1h ago”, the forecast figures and other 0.76–0.82rem labels moved by about a pixel.
  • Not visible here: the priority queue (in Advanced diagnostics) lost its Snooze button and the “Audit script” download is gone.

/users — mobile 390×844

  • Unchanged apart from the “read Xm ago” time: the 7/30/90-day picker now uses the shared .app-segmented class that /settings also uses.
